name: Syracuse Orange
lede: Syracuse Orange is the burnt, reddish orange of Syracuse University's teams, a school color rather than a pigment or dye name.

sections.title: A university's orange
sections.body:
Our library traces the name only to a Wikipedia color list, which credits Syracuse University but gives no date for when the school adopted this exact shade [1]. The name itself is a school's branding word, not a material, place of origin or person [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[sinopia]], 2.7 units of CIEDE2000 away and described as almost the same [2]. [[sinopia]] sits a little farther out at 3.8, duller, [[burnt-orange]] at 4.7, also duller, and [[mars-orange]] at 4.9, also duller [2]. Measured in LCH it reads lightness 50, chroma 81, a saturated orange leaning toward red [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 49 of 23,781 paintings (0.21 percent), more common than 51 percent of the named colors, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1400s, in 7 of 945 paintings from that century, 1.7 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it plays an accent in all of the matched works, a role measured by lightness rank within the canvas [3]. The earliest dated match is 1400, by the Master of Rubielos de Mora, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
